name: Omnitree Refinement
definition: Omnitrees partition a d-dimensional Cartesian domain Ω ⊂ R^d into N nonoverlapping subdomains Q_i, where boundaries occur at dyadic rationals (multiples of 2^-k). An omnitree node v is characterized by a binary splitting label b(v) ∈ {0, 1}^d, where b_j = 1 indicates bisection in dimension j, yielding 2^|σ(v)| children. The all-zero label b = 0 is reserved for leaf nodes. Normalization enforces that splits are gathered as high in the tree as possible, guaranteeing a unique, shallowest representation.
summary: Omnitree Refinement transforms a hierarchical dyadic partition into a target partition with higher resolution in specific dimensions, supporting non-cubic, rectangular subdomains via per-dimension refinement markers.
